name: introspection
description: tables/schema/dump op behavior with two tables: tables lists names alphabetically, schema (no argument) lists CREATE statements in creation order (not alphabetical -- deliberately checked so a future reordering is caught), schema with a table argument filters to one, and dump's pattern parameter filters which table's data/DDL is included. Also checks the stable fields of inspect right after a fresh start with no snapshot loaded -- inspect reflects the running binary's own embedded data (protocol.md: inspect は自プロセスの状態のみ), not live SQL state mutated via exec, so has_data/data_length/version stay at their empty defaults even after CREATE TABLE. The `source` field is deliberately not asserted here: it echoes the invoked binary's own argv[0] basename, which is not stable across how a runner launches the process.

request.sql: CREATE TABLE users(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)
CREATE TABLE logs(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, msg TEXT)

schema: CREATE TABLE users(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)
CREATE TABLE logs(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, msg TEXT)
CREATE TABLE users(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)
